phase: Baseline (before any lab): phase 1 automated checks, plus gate status where the evidence already decides it

audited.environment: Linux workspace, Node 22.22.0, PostgreSQL 16 for the database tests; setup evidence from macOS (Oct 20 to 22) where stated

profile.users: Businesses (small agencies), multi-user, data separated by workspace
profile.hosting: Local only; the as-built version is never deployed

verdict.summary: Every L1 gate passes. The app is held at L1 by three L2 gates that no code change can satisfy on its own: backups with a performed restore, an error tracker, and CI that can block a merge.

gates.evidence: gitleaks over full history (6 commits): no leaks; gitleaks over .next/static: no leaks; AGENTS.md has no key/token/secret lines; only .env.example is tracked
Signed-out /clients returns 307 to /login; signed-out API returns 401. Full route inventory is phase 2
No critical advisories. npm audit on macOS (Oct 20): 5 high, all dev-only lint tooling; npm audit in the Linux workspace (Oct 26): 0. Production dependencies: 0 in both
Fresh clone at v0-as-built: npm ci, type check, lint and production build all exit 0; README steps worked end to end on macOS (setup, Oct 22)
Design looks right (server actions re-read workspace and role; billing columns not writable by the browser role, covered by DB tests). Per-route review of write handlers is phase 2
RLS on all 9 tables; 48 database tests, including cross-workspace reads and writes, pass against real Postgres
Rate limits on login, sign-up and the brief endpoint; login limiter covered by DB tests
zod schemas with size caps and page-size caps exist and have unit tests; coverage of every write route is phase 2
Monthly per-workspace cap (atomic reserve, DB-tested), 25 s timeout, 700 max output tokens, rate limits on the endpoint
Signature verified on every event; duplicate, concurrent and stale events tested against real Postgres; live test-mode webhooks returned 200 on macOS (Oct 22)
122 tests pass: 74 unit, 48 against real Postgres covering auth, isolation and the money path
dependabot.yml present (weekly npm and Actions). Age of the 5 dev-only high advisories seen on macOS not yet checked against the 30-day rule
Production build serves nonce-based CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options and X-Content-Type-Options; cross-site POST returns 403
No tools given to the model; output rendered as React text nodes only (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML or markdown rendering in src); untrusted notes wrapped and escaped. Adversarial testing is Lab 7
No TODO, FIXME, mock or sample-data markers in src; no empty catch blocks

findings.title: No backups and no restore has ever been performed
findings.location: No backup configuration in the repo; README 'What's not built yet' lists no backups policy
findings.failure_scenario: A bad migration or deleted workspace on a hosted database cannot be recovered, and nobody knows how long recovery would take
findings.fix: Enable backups on the hosted Supabase project, perform one restore into a scratch project and record the date and result

findings.title: Errors are scrubbed but go only to stderr; no error tracker
findings.failure_scenario: A production error affecting customers is written to a log nobody watches
findings.fix: Wire setErrorSink to an error tracker, keep the scrubbing, send one test event and keep the record

findings.title: CI exists but cannot block a merge
findings.location: .github/workflows/ci.yml; no GitHub remote or branch protection
findings.failure_scenario: A change that fails type checks or tests is merged because nothing requires the checks to pass
findings.fix: Push to GitHub, require the CI job as a status check on main, and record the protection settings

findings.title: CI workflow file is invalid YAML, so no CI check has ever run
findings.failure_scenario: Every push and pull request shows CI as failed before any job starts, so type check, lint, tests and build never run on GitHub and a broken change looks no different from a good one
findings.found: 2026-10-29, first CI run on GitHub after the repo went public; missed by the Oct 26 baseline, which only checked that the file existed
findings.fix: Quote the step name, validate the workflow (actionlint) in the baseline script, and confirm a green run before requiring it in branch protection

findings.title: CODEOWNERS names a placeholder; human review of agent changes is not enforced
findings.failure_scenario: An AI agent's change reaches main without any human reading it
findings.fix: Replace the placeholder with a real owner and turn on 'Require review from Code Owners'; scope agent credentials so they cannot push to main

findings.title: Health check exists but no alert reaches a named person
findings.failure_scenario: The app or its database goes down and the first person to notice is a customer
findings.fix: Point an uptime monitor at /api/health and route alerts to a named owner

findings.title: No deploy pipeline and no tested rollback
findings.location: No deploy configuration; deployment is out of scope per README
findings.failure_scenario: A bad release cannot be rolled back quickly, so an outage lasts as long as a fix takes to write
findings.fix: Deploy the hardened version through a pipeline with preview deploys, then perform and record one rollback

findings.title: No restore drill against stated RTO and RPO
findings.location: No RTO/RPO targets or drill record
findings.failure_scenario: Nobody can tell a buyer how much data could be lost or how long recovery takes
findings.fix: Set RTO and RPO targets, run a timed restore drill and record it (Lab 5)

findings.title: Secrets live in local .env files; no secrets manager, rotation or per-person access
findings.location: src/lib/env.ts reads process.env; README lists secrets management as out of scope
findings.failure_scenario: A key shared between people cannot be rotated without coordination, and nobody can say who has it
findings.fix: Store production secrets in the hosting platform's secret store or a secrets manager, with per-person access and a rotation record

findings.title: Data flows to Stripe and Anthropic are documented, but there is no subprocessor list
findings.location: README 'Data sent to third parties'; README 'What's not built yet' lists no DPA/subprocessor documentation
findings.failure_scenario: A buyer's questionnaire asks for subprocessors and the LLM provider is missing or undocumented
findings.fix: Publish a subprocessor list (Supabase, Stripe, Anthropic, hosting) with purpose, data and region, and record each provider's data-use terms

findings.title: Per-IP rate limits trust X-Forwarded-For
findings.failure_scenario: Without a trusted proxy setting the header, a client can rotate the header to dodge per-IP limits; per-email limits still apply
findings.fix: Read the client IP only from the deployment platform's trusted header

findings.title: Dev-only high advisories; audit results differ by environment
findings.location: npm audit: 5 high (braces via eslint-config-next) on macOS Oct 20; 0 in the Linux workspace Oct 26
findings.failure_scenario: Dependency evidence that changes with where and when it runs cannot support a 30-day remediation rule
findings.fix: Run npm audit in CI on a schedule, keep the dated output as evidence, and track advisory age

findings.title: Built on Supabase's legacy anon and service_role keys
findings.failure_scenario: Key names in the docs don't match what the current Supabase CLI shows, and the legacy keys can't be rotated independently
findings.fix: Move to Supabase publishable and secret keys and update the docs

findings.title: README is behind reality
findings.location: README 'Running tests' says the Supabase Postgres (54322) hasn't been tried; 'What's not built yet' says the app has never run against real Supabase, Stripe or Anthropic
findings.failure_scenario: Readers follow a harder path than needed and distrust a README that contradicts what the app has since done
findings.fix: Update both statements with the dates and results of the Oct 20 to 22 setup
